articles.title: Lanterns Showrunner on Episode 2’s Big Ending: ‘When and Where to Use the Ring Is the Whole Ballgame’
articles.summary: Full spoilers follow for HBO’s Lanterns Episode 2. After last week’s premiere episode of Lanterns – the latest show in James Gunn and Peter Safran’s DC Universe – got some fans fuming and others interested thanks to the radical decision to kill off legendary Green Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler)…
body: At first glance, this show could be confused with being just another detective series set in smalltown USA. But then a scene like the one that ends Episode 2 happens, and there’s no doubt that this is the space cop Green Lantern, a guy who can fly to another planet at the drop of a hat.

“It's like Kyle says in the bar in the pilot, ‘When and where to use the ring is the whole ballgame,’” showrunner Chris Mundy told me when I asked him about the use of the Green Lantern ring on the show. For him and his team, the decision on when to use it, and when not to use it, was not taken lightly.

“That was a character thing for Hal, but it was also sort of us talking to ourselves a little bit,” he continued. “We wanted to earn the times we used it in a big way. We start small and start kind of playful with the $20 bill and all those kinds of things, so that each time we used it, people trusted us, like, ‘Oh, they're not just plastering everything with it all the time.’ It's those characters [deciding when to use it], and then because of that, those writers who are making those characters do that thing, they know when to employ it and when not to.”

articles.title: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 2 Review & Recap
articles.summary: Lanterns continues to impress in its sophomore episode, proving that Kyle Chandler’s Hal and Aaron Pierre’s John are just as entertaining apart as they are together. Read our full review of Episode 2.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 2!

Lanterns got a lot of things right in its pilot episode, but above all, the series benefited from the compelling chemistry between Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart. These two can barely tolerate one another at the best of times, and it makes for a hell of a lot of fun. But what happens when the follow-up episode splits this Dynamic Duo up for the majority of its runtime? As it turns out, these two characters are just as fascinating apart as they are together.

Episode 2 features some terrific Hal/John scenes as bookends, but for the most part, the emphasis is on the two men as solo players. While John carries out a glorified fetch quest for his grouchy mentor, Hal sets about digging deeper into the mysteries of Rushville, Nebraska. Needless to say, both men wind up discovering far more than they bargained for in the end.
points: Lanterns continues to impress in its sophomore episode, proving that Kyle Chandler’s Hal and Aaron Pierre’s John are just as entertaining apart as they are together.

articles.title: 5 Strongest Characters In Kaiju No. 8
articles.summary: Such is also the case in Naoya Matsumoto’s Kaiju No. 8, which is set in a world where monsters named kaiju regularly trigger disasters. Apart from the kaiju themselves, we have to take the Japanese Anti-Kaiju Defense Force into consideration, as these skilled combatants are specifically trained to…
body: Strength is a fickle thing in any action fantasy setting. A powerful character might win or lose a fight for all sorts of reasons. That’s doubly true in anime, where character abilities evolve over time, and some power-ups might be fueled purely by emotional states.

The destructive powers of a kaiju are measured via an assigned fortitude level. This also determines their class, like the stronger, more dangerous honju and the smaller yoju. Sometimes, kaiju develop fortitude levels that are considered abnormal, which earns them the classification of daikaiju. To even the playing field, members of the Defense Force fortify their powered suits with kaiju remains, which determines their strength, speed, and durability during combat. As these factors also rely on individual skill and experience, powerscaling characters in Kaiju No. 8 might feel subjective or tricky.
With this in mind, here are the five strongest characters in the Kaiju No. 8 manga and anime, ranked.

articles.title: HBO Officially Changes a Fundamental Rule of DC Superhero Canon
articles.summary: In 2014’s Justice League: War, heroes including Superman, Wonder Woman, and the Flash unite to defend Earth from an invasion led by Darkseid. Batman and Green Lantern are among the first to stumble into an uneasy partnership.
body: Adapted from Geoff Johns and Jim Lee’s 2011 Justice League #1, the scene is a funny distillation of both characters. Hal is powerful and cocky. Batman is observant enough to identify and steal the source of that power within minutes. It also dramatizes one of the Green Lantern mythology’s basic rules: The ring transforms willpower into physical hard-light constructs, but a Lantern has to be wearing the ring to wield that power.
HBO’s Lanterns just pushed that rule to its apparent limit — and potentially set John Stewart up to become the most powerful Green Lantern in the DC Universe.

In Lanterns episode 2, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) maintains an intricate, autonomous construct while separated from the ring and after repeatedly losing consciousness. The Green Lantern comics contain a handful of comparable feats, but they usually involve veteran Lanterns, unusual rings, or cosmic transformations. John accomplishes it after just two months of training, which already makes him seem like a prodigy among the Corps.

articles.title: The Batman: Part 2 Set Videos Show Batmobile Clashing With Gotham Police
articles.summary: User videos of the Batmobile first surfaced online last week. More recently, a mysterious blonde woman was spotted in the Batmobile's passenger seat. (Was it Scarlett Johansson?
body: Now, multiple videos have appeared across social media showing the roaring Batmobile doing donuts on the (fake) snowy streets of Glasgow, er, Gotham City, Gotham City police vehicles chasing it, the GCPD surrounding the Batmobile, and SWAT officers opening fire on it at point blank range. A SWAT vehicle was also spotted ramming the Batmobile at one point.

Director Matt Reeves’ The Batman portrayed a tense but ultimately fruitful alliance between the Caped Crusader and the GCPD, particularly with Lt. Jim Gordon. The film’s ending showed Batman saving the mayor and other citizens from the Riddler. Public sentiment about Batman seemed to be turning in the superhero’s favor.

So now, seeing the police chasing and firing at the Batmobile clearly shows the alliance between Batman and the GCPD has deteriorated. Batman is being treated as an outlaw. Whether this also puts Batman at odds with Gordon personally remains to be seen.
Do you think Batman’s been framed here? Or has the Dark Knight taken matters into his own hands too much for Gotham’s powers-that-be to allow? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: ‘Lanterns’ Episode 2 Ending Explained: Who Are Sinestro and the Manhunters?
articles.summary: HBO’s Lanterns is taking a very grounded approach to its portrayal of DC ’s galactic peacekeeper Green Lantern. The TV series is mostly set in the dusty town of Rushville, Nebraska, and it’s more focused on buddy cop dynamics and True Detective -style mystery than superhero action.
body: In episode 2, Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) sends his trainee John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) back to his home in Coast City to recharge his power ring and feed his carnivorous alien plant. John is abducted outside Hal’s home by aliens, part of the same group involved in the mass shooting that brought the Green Lantern to Rushville. Their leader, Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor), says they are looking for a Manhunter, which he describes as “one of the most dangerous beings to ever exist.”

Since the Manhunter has taken human form, Antaan explains he can be killed as a human. Antaan plans to blow up the whole town in 48 hours if John doesn’t find the Manhunter before then. Antaan is disappointed by John’s education as a prospective Green Lantern, pointing out Hal should have told John how impressive it is that he can maintain his bird construct without even wearing the ring. He’s also surprised he doesn’t know who the Manhunters are. “You think the Green Lanterns came first? You really don’t know?” Antaan asks.

articles.title: 7 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics With No Words
articles.summary: When it comes to comedic outlets — be it a movie, a sitcom, a comedy troupe, or even just a single comedian — it’s rare to be a master of both subtle humor and broad, unsubtle comedy. The Three Stooges, for example, are delightfully unsubtle in their brand of violent physical comedy.
body: There are exceptions, though. The Marx brothers are an example of a comedy troupe that could do both. Groucho Marx could deliver a thoughtful quip that might take a second to decode, while Harpo Marx could do something blatantly silly, like getting caught stealing silverware. On a good episode of the sitcom Frasier, David Hyde Pierce’s portrayal of Niles Crane would feature delightful wordplay in one scene and buffoonish physical comedy in the next.
The Far Side cartoonist Gary Larson is similarly a master of both subtle comedy and humor that was wonderfully uncomplicated.

From 1980 until 1995, his single-panel newspaper comic strip featured Larson’s uniquely subversive and silly brand of humor with new characters and scenarios in every strip. Some were broad sight gags that even a young child could enjoy, whereas others could be incredibly understated, and act a bit like a comedy puzzle, where the reader had to examine them to find the joke. Both ends of Larson’s spectrum were hilarious, and that's what kept the comic strip fresh for 15 years.
points: When it comes to comedic outlets — be it a movie, a sitcom, a comedy troupe, or even just a single comedian — it’s rare to be a master of both subtle humor and broad, unsubtle comedy.
The Three Stooges, for example, are delightfully unsubtle in their brand of violent physical comedy.
The Marx brothers are an example of a comedy troupe that could do both.

articles.title: Nightdive's Thief remaster unearths a 'very very out of date version control repository' with 'the wildest things to say about the code'
articles.summary: It's great that the Nightdive's remasters of various classic games give new players a chance to experience them without having to download a fixpack or remap the controls or whatever, but it's also a wonderful opportunity to learn new things about games we already loved.
body: Digital Foundry's Retro Super Show recently spoke to Nightdive about their current project, a remaster of Looking Glass Studio's stealth classic Thief: The Dark Project. If you're super into the minutiae of Thief, as you should be, it's a cool insight into the making of the game and in particular, the Dark Engine that powers it.

"There's nothing else like it even to this day," Nightdive software engineer Josh Dowell says. As he explains, Nightdive got to see "a very very out of date version control repository for the code" and that made the origins of its oddities more obvious. "I think most of the team that started working on it ended up moving to different projects and then a whole new team took over for the second half of its development," he says.

articles.title: Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 Controller Is Still Available for Preorder (But It May Sell Out)
articles.summary: The big PS5 exclusive this fall is Marvel’s Wolverine. It’s Insomniac Studios’ follow-up to the excellent (and massively successful) Spider-Man games, and it promises to be a bloody good time.
body: Functionally, Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Wireless Controller is a standard PS5 controller. What makes it stand out is the design, which makes it look like Wolverine got mad while playing Fortnite and attacked the thing. It features three jagged claw marks across the face of the controller. The marks are vibrant yellow, set against the black of the grips and touchpad. It looks fierce.

The bottom of the controller is also yellow, as are the shapes on the face buttons and the tiny arrows on the D-pad. On the left and right grips you’ll also find gray scuff marks that add to the battle-damage effect. Overall, it’s one of the coolest PS5 controller designs yet — and there have been a lot.

The controller actually comes in two variations. There’s a “Battle Yellow” one that’s bright and bold. Then there’s an “Adamantium” white one that features the same scuffed-and-clawed design, but with metallic white to accent the black, making it somewhat less flashy. The Adamantium white one was a PlayStation Direct exclusive, and it has, unfortunately, sold out.

It’s Insomniac Studios’ follow-up to the excellent (and massively successful) Spider-Man games, and it promises to be a bloody good time.

articles.title: Steam Week in Review: A touch of AI is all it takes to trigger backlash, as a promising new indie falls afoul of slop skeptics
articles.summary: All the interesting Steam facts for the week ending August 23
body: Vapor World: Over The Mind is a Soulslike Metroidvania with an evocative, painterly art style reminiscent of Lies of P and the narrative platformers of Playdead. According to Korean studio Alive Inc, the game had 100,000 wishlists just before its early access launch on August 19, mostly on the strength of a demo available since January 2025.

But what should have been a triumphant early access launch went pear shaped very quickly. At launch, few talked about the quite distinctive worldbuilding or the parry-heavy combat. Instead, all focus was trained entirely on something absent from the popular demo: very obvious AI use.

"Saw the very first cutscene, before any gameplay, and how the generative AI they used couldn't even keep the main character's model consistent," reads the "most helpful" Steam review for Vapor World. "From the trailers the gameplay looked pretty fun [but] unfortunately I support people not robots. If the look you want to go for is beyond the scope you can achieve right now then I suggest you change it or wait until you can produce the art and style you want with people doing it."

articles.title: Twitch faces a class action lawsuit over using streamers' content to train Amazon's AI
articles.summary: A Twitch streamer has filed a proposed class action against the platform and its parent company Amazon, claiming his broadcasts, and those of countless other creators, were fed into generative AI training with neither consent nor payment.
body: According to Courthouse News, plaintiff Warren Pandiscia – a Twitch creator with around 1000 followers – filed his 37-page complaint in the Northern District of California last week. It alleges Twitch and Amazon copied vast quantities of streamer footage without securing proper licences, a breach of creators' implied agreements with the platform and a violation of state unfair competition law.

Twitch announced it would start training generative AI models on the platform earlier this month. Its community of streamers immediately pushed back, with demands that these AI features be optional the most popular request by miles. Streamers demanded to know why this feature was on by default, forcing users to manually go into the settings to opt out from generative AI training.

Chief product officer Mike Minton offered a surprisingly candid response to this question, insisting that "if it was opt in, nobody would opt in. So it's going to be on by default, and almost every content service in the world is on by default".

articles.title: Epic Games Store overhaul might be "too little, too late", says Newzoo analyst
articles.summary: While Epic has spent much of this year promising a launcher overhaul, including a faster, redesigned storefront with tailored recommendations and quicker ways to browse, one industry analyst has revealed that it might not be enough.
body: Speaking to PC Gamer, Emmanuel Rosier, director of market intelligence at Newzoo, admitted, "I don't see how they can recover at this point".

Rosier's argument centres on Steam's unshakeable grip on the market, with Epic's free game giveaways doing little to build lasting engagement, pointing out that a giveaway can sometimes end up boosting a game's sales on Steam instead, as players stick to one launcher rather than fragment their collection.

"I don't really see how they can turn that around because Steam has become so inevitable," he said. "The Epic Games Store, they get players by giving free games, but people just go, they log in, they get the free games, they don't even play them. You know, it's almost like collecting games rather than actually playing them.

"The challenge I think Epic is facing is that they try to win everywhere in the past few years," Rosier added. "They try to win against Steam, they try to win against Apple, against Google Play, and probably they run out of steam on where they cannot fight all these battles at the same time."

articles.title: PSA: Modern Warfare 4's Switch 2 Retail Version Is Apparently A Code-In-A-Box
articles.summary: It's just a box with a download code, according to VGP. If you're wondering how exactly Activision will distribute the retail version of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on the Switch 2, some new information has surfaced via social media. This update comes from Video Games Plus.
body: This update comes from Video Games Plus. According to the North American physical video game distributor, the Switch 2 version of MW4 will be a "code-in-box" release when it arrives this October. As it's "just a box with a download code inside", VGP says it won't be carrying the product.

This might not be the most surprising news if you're familiar with how the series operates nowadays, but it's still caused some upset online. Activision's file sizes, downloads and updates for the blockbuster titles have continued to rise, and existing releases have been managed through a dedicated game launcher, where you select what games, modes and content to install.

There's no official update about how exactly the installation for the Switch 2 version of the game will work, but this will be the first Call of Duty on a Nintendo platform in 13 years, so any file management will focus exclusively on this title. In early access on Switch 2, players simply download and launch the beta to play it.

articles.title: 'We didn't have layoffs before, and now all of a sudden we have yearly layoffs': Bethesda artist says 'something has changed' under Microsoft
articles.summary: Last week, the Communications Workers of America and the Bethesda Game Studios OneBGS union took part in the Save Our Devs rally across the United States and Canada (and on Twitch ) "to call out layoffs and corporate greed across the industry and to demand fair first contracts across Microsoft’s…
body: "Since we’ve been under Microsoft… it feels like something has changed. We didn’t have layoffs before, and now all of a sudden we have yearly layoffs," he told Kotaku, saying teams were feeling the effects of cuts which eroded institutional knowledge. “If only five people knew how this thing worked and you let all five of them go, that’s a morale killer because it’s like we already knew this, and now we have to learn it again.”

According to that article, Nguyen pointed out that fixer-uppers like Fallout 76 and Elder Scrolls Online don't get a chance to bloom into successful fan favorites without sufficient labor and time. He also noted that there used to be a shared sense of long-term commitment among the staff at Zenimax and Bethesda—a commitment being smothered by Microsoft's current corporate tactics.

“That’s why a lot of people had such a long tenure here," Nguyen told Kotaku. "And they were like, ‘yeah, this is the place I’m gonna retire at,’ or ‘this is the place where I’m gonna finish out,’ or ‘I love being here because I want to stay in the industry for a long time.’ That was basically one of the benefits of being at Bethesda or a Zenimax studio in general.”

articles.title: Miyazaki explains how The Duskbloods plans to protect newcomers from its best players
articles.summary: FromSoftware is stepping into one of multiplayer gaming's most divisive arguments with The Duskbloods, confirming the upcoming Switch 2 exclusive will lean on skill-based matchmaking to keep newcomers safe from its most battle-hardened players.
body: Speaking to IGN, FromSoftware president and Duskbloods director Hidetaka Miyazaki confirmed the game will run on a ranked system, pairing highly skilled players together and keeping newer players in their own pool specifically to avoid lopsided matches as the game's skill gap widens over time.

Skill-based matchmaking has been a persistent flashpoint in multiplayer games for years. Games like Call of Duty and Apex Legends have repeatedly faced backlash from players who feel it makes lobbies feel unnecessarily punishing.

"In terms of really, really good players, we definitely plan on having the matchmaking system work in a way so that it's ranked, and players who are really good tend to be matched with other players who are great, and players who are new tend to be matched with other new players just to avoid situations like you had mentioned," he explained.

videos.title: Metal Gear Solid 4: The Flawed Masterpiece Kojima Didn't Want to Make
videos.summary: Trapped on the dead PS3 no more, Metal Gear Solid 4 is a late 2000s fossil inbound to current-gen hardware and PCs thanks to the Master Collection Volume 2, but is Hideo Kojima's flawed masterpiece, one he didn't even want to make in the first place, still worth playing in 2026?
points: Trapped on the dead PS3 no more, Metal Gear Solid 4 is a late 2000s fossil inbound to current-gen hardware and PCs thanks to the Master Collection Volume 2, but is Hideo Kojima's flawed masterpiece…
Grab your nanomachine-packed syringe, power on that iPod, and relax, as we sneak our way through a retrospective packed with Old Snake's buttcheeks, military jargon and a boatload of lore.
This is Kojima's wayward masterpiece; this is Guns of the Patriots.
videos.author: IGN
